title: Duet: A Collaborative User Driven Recommendation System for Edge Devices
problem: Recommendation models are compute and memory-intensive, making them unsuitable for direct deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. The full model cannot fit or execute efficiently on edge hardware while maintaining acceptable latency.
motivation: Enabling efficient recommendation inference at the edge reduces latency and energy consumption for user-facing applications by eliminating full cloud dependency.
method: Duet splits a recommendation model into two pieces: a user model (which learns from your history and profile) that runs on your local edge device, and an item model (which learns about products or content) that runs in the cloud. These two parts run at the same time. The user part is optimized to use less computing power so it fits on edge hardware with its limited resources, and then their outputs are combined to make the final recommendation.
key_novelty: The core idea is splitting a recommendation model into user and item parts that run simultaneously on edge devices and the cloud, combining their results, instead of keeping the entire model in one place.
contributions: Decomposition strategy separating user history/attributes from item-related computations for edge-cloud split execution
Lightweight edge device architecture enabling user model deployment on resource-constrained hardware
6.4X average latency reduction through intelligent workload distribution
4.6X energy efficiency improvement across five recommendation model architectures
